questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2 \\ 5{x}_{2}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+2(2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+2=0.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 5 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 5 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 22 & 22 \\ 0 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{3}{22}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 22 & 22 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ 22{x}_{2}=22.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+4(1)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2+1=-1.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 11 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 11 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 11 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=6 \\ -{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-7 \\ -3{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second   equation yields

$$
-{x}_{2}-2(2)=-7\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=3$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(3)+2=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

So, we have ${x}_{1}=1.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 15 \\ 12\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 15 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 15 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 15 \\ 0 & 4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 15 \\ 0 & 0 & -9 & -27\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3 \\ 2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=15 \\ -9{x}_{3}=-27.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=3.$ Substituting this into the second   equation yields

$$
2{x}_{2}+3(3)=15\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=3$ and ${x}_{3}=3$ into the first equation we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3+3=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

So, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3+3+3=9.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -8 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,-8\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,-7\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=(-8)\cdot {b}_{1}+(-7)\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{2}=-7.$
